meta.disclaimer: On-the-ground conditions change quickly — fuel queues, power cuts, and ATM outages are localised. Use this as planning context and confirm with your lodge or host on arrival.

topics.title: Power & load shedding
topics.body: National load shedding has been suspended for extended periods since mid-2025 as Eskom's generation recovery improves. However, localised load reduction still affects some high-density areas with illegal connections. Upmarket lodges and hotels usually have generators or inverters — ask when booking. Apps like EskomSePush help monitor your suburb if staying in self-catering accommodation.

topics.title: Cash vs cards
topics.body: Cards widely accepted in cities, malls, and SANParks online. Carry cash for township tours, tips, and rural fuel stops. Contactless payment common in Cape Town and Johannesburg.

topics.title: Plugs
topics.body: Type M (three round pins, 230V) — same as Namibia and much of the region. Type C also fits many sockets. Bring a universal adapter.

topics.title: Fuel
topics.body: Generally reliable on main routes. Unleaded 95/93 at Engen, Shell, BP. SANRAL e-tags speed Gauteng tolls — rental companies can advise.

topics.title: Fuel & distances
topics.body: Fill at every town — distances between pumps on B1 and C-roads are extreme. Carry at least 400 km range on gravel routes. 95 octane available in Windhoek, Swakopmund, Otjiwarongo; some remote posts 93 only.

topics.title: Money
topics.body: Namibian dollar pegged 1:1 to ZAR — both accepted. Cards work in towns; cash for community conservancy gate fees and remote camps.

topics.title: Plugs
topics.body: Type M (230V). Solar lodges may have limited 220V hours — charge devices at midday.

topics.title: Driving
topics.body: Never drive after dark outside towns — kudu strikes on tar are common. Two spare tyres recommended for Damaraland and Kaokoland.

topics.title: Cash vs cards
topics.body: Pula cash useful at small shops. Cards accepted in Maun, Kasane, and Gaborone. Okavango camps are mostly pre-paid — minimal spending on site.

topics.title: IDP
topics.body: International Driving Permit strongly recommended for all foreign drivers — police and rental desks often request it.

topics.title: Plugs
topics.body: Type G (British three-pin) in many lodges; Type M also seen. Confirm with your camp.

topics.title: Connectivity
topics.body: Orange and BTC SIMs work in gateway towns. Delta camps rely on satellite Wi‑Fi — download maps offline.

topics.title: Cash & KAZA
topics.body: USD cash essential for KAZA UniVisa (USD 50) and Victoria Falls activities. Kwacha for local markets. ATMs in Lusaka and Livingstone.

topics.title: Plugs
topics.body: Type C, D, and G — mixed. Universal adapter required.

topics.title: Fuel
topics.body: Generally available on Great North Road and to Mfuwe. Remote bushcamps accessed by air — no self-drive fuel needed.

topics.title: Mobile money
topics.body: Airtel and MTN mobile money widely used domestically — tourists usually pay USD or kwacha cash at lodges.

topics.title: USD economy
topics.body: Tourism priced in USD — carry small, clean notes ($1, $5, $10, $20). ZiG used locally but USD simplest for visitors. Change is often scarce — break large notes at hotels.

topics.title: Fuel
topics.body: Availability has improved but queues still occur in Harare and Bulawayo. Fill before Hwange and Mana Pools loops. USD cash sometimes required at pumps.

topics.title: Plugs
topics.body: Type D and G (220V). UK-style plugs common in Victoria Falls hotels.

topics.title: Connectivity
topics.body: Econet and NetOne SIMs in Victoria Falls and Harare. Hwange lodges have patchy signal — do not rely on mobile data for navigation.

topics.title: Money
topics.body: Metical for local spending; USD accepted at tourist lodges. Visa more widely accepted than a few years ago — carry metical cash for road tolls and markets.

topics.title: Plugs
topics.body: Type C, F, and M — European two-pin most common. 220V.

topics.title: Coastal travel
topics.body: Cyclone season Jan–Mar affects north. Police checkpoints on EN1 — keep passport, insurance, and temporary import permit accessible.

topics.title: Driving
topics.body: Do not drive at night — livestock, unlit vehicles, and potholes on EN1. Maputo traffic heavy; allow border time at Ressano Garcia.

topics.title: Fuel
topics.body: Periodic shortages — fill tank at Lilongwe or Blantyre before lake shore drives. Carry enough cash for fuel in case card systems fail.

topics.title: Cash
topics.body: Kwacha from ATMs in cities. USD useful for park fees and tipping. Lake shore lodges may prefer cash.

topics.title: Plugs
topics.body: Type G (British three-pin, 230V).

topics.title: Lake swimming
topics.body: Bilharzia risk in reedy bays — ask lodge staff before swimming. Cape Maclear and Likoma have safer known spots.

topics.title: Fuel
topics.body: No fuel on Sani Pass or remote highlands — fill in Maseru, Hlotse, or SA before ascending. Maseru Bridge border from Ladybrand is the main entry.

topics.title: Mountain passes
topics.body: Sani Pass 4x4 only (SA side). Snow closes passes Jun–Aug some years. Pony trekking villages have no ATM — carry loti cash.

topics.title: Plugs
topics.body: Type M (same as South Africa).

topics.title: Entry
topics.body: Landlocked — all access via South Africa. Ensure SA visa allows multiple entries if looping back.

topics.title: Getting there
topics.body: No commercial international airport — fly to Johannesburg (JNB) or Durban (DUR). Oshoek/Ngwenya border 2.5 hrs from JNB to Mbabane; Golela from KZN to lowveld reserves.

topics.title: Roads
topics.body: Among the best in the region — tar throughout Ezulwini Valley and to Hlane. SA rental with cross-border letter required.

topics.title: Money
topics.body: Lilangeni pegged 1:1 to ZAR — rand accepted everywhere. Cards in Mbabane and Ezulwini; cash for craft markets.

topics.title: Plugs
topics.body: Type M (230V) — same as South Africa.
